newsitem.title: USA: U.S. banks earn $13.8 billion in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. banks earn $13.8 billion in second quarter.

text.p: The nation's 9,689 commercial banks earned $13.8 billion in the second quarter, up from $12 billion a year earlier, regulators said Wednesday.
But the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. also reported an increase in credit quality problems in banks' loans to individuals, especially credit-card loans.
Last quarter's results were the second-highest ever and represented only the second time the industry's profits have exceeded $13 billion.

"The earnings of commercial banks have never been better," FDIC Chairman Ricki Helfer told a news conference. "If the commerical banking industry maintains the earnings strength it displayed during the first half of 1996 for the next six months, it will -- for the first time ever -- earn more than $50 billion in one year."
Banks earned $25.5 billion in the first half of 1996, up $2.4 billion from the first half of 1995.
The FDIC attributed last quarter's performance to gains associated with bank mergers and industry consolidation, as well as increases in income derived from fees.

Not all the news was positive. Banks wrote off $3.8 billion in loans in the second quarter, $1 billion more than a year earlier. It was the second highest quarterly amount charged off in the last 10 quarters.
The increase in loan losses was largely due to charge-offs on loans to individuals. Charge-off rates on these loans rose to 2.24 percent in the second quarter from 1.40 percent two years earlier.
The FDIC added that net charge-offs on bank credit-card loans accounted for almost two-thirds of all loan losses in the second quarter.
The FDIC counted 99 banks on its list of "problem" institutions, down from 127 at the end of the first quarter.
